headline: AMD's chief executive said demand for its AI chips will stay very high for years and called on big AI companies to cooperate.
score_reason: Lowered from 7: mostly a repeat of our 6 Oct Reuters story; the new part is the call for cooperation, which is thinly reported.
importance_line: If demand outruns supply for several years, buyers of AI computing may keep facing tight supply and high prices, but the reports give no figures and the cooperation call is only briefly described.
summary: Bloomberg and Reuters report that AMD chief executive Lisa Su, speaking in Taiwan, said AMD will raise its chip supply substantially in 2027 because demand for its processors still exceeds what it can make. New since our 6 Oct edition, which carried Reuters on the supply plan, Su urged major AI companies to cooperate more on safety, and AMD is now planning three to five years ahead and needs more advanced wafer capacity (the silicon discs chips are cut from).
notes: Bloomberg page blocked (robot check). Text read: GuruFocus summary on TradingView (secondary, unsourced to Bloomberg) plus Reuters headline from Google News. Safety wording of the cooperation call comes from that summary only; Bloomberg's own wording unseen. Follows C08-01 of the 6 Oct edition.
